clue.text: Weapon thought right to be carried by sergeant-major

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it, so these pieces go inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a thought is an idea

explanation.surface: A soldier's weapon is judged fit to be borne by the sergeant-major.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol or other small firearm worn at the belt is a soldier's personal weapon.

clue.text: Carton dispatched in error by the French

definitions.text: Carton dispatched in error by the French

parts.words: Carton dispatched in error by the French
parts.note: Dickens's hero in A Tale of Two Cities goes to the guillotine in Paris in another man's place; the clue asks for his first name, which is also an Australian city

explanation.surface: A cardboard box was sent off by mistake by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carton' looks like a box, but it is Dickens's character, guillotined by the French revolutionaries instead of Charles Darnay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tale of Two Cities hero's given name is that of the New South Wales capital, and the novel's executed lawyer bears it.

clue.text: Removal of single vessel in gloomy situation

indicators.note: the single and the vessel are placed inside the gloomy word

parts.note: a dismal situation is a gloomy one; dismal means gloomy
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: Taking away a lone ship in bleak circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacking or sending away is the act of removing someone from a post.

clue.text: In the style of scholars in Birmingham area

parts.note: a la is the French borrowing meaning in the style of
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar
MA, Master of Arts, is a second graduate scholar

explanation.surface: Something in the manner of the academics at a Midlands university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birmingham' suggests the English city, but there is a large Birmingham in the American South too; two degrees give the two scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern US state contains a major city called Birmingham, so the state is the area around it.

clue.text: Soaked before eating, dine drunkenly with a dram

indicators.note: a drunken arrangement staggers the letters of the words around it into a new order

explanation.surface: Tipsy diners have had a whisky with their meal, soaked before dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Food steeped in a seasoned liquid before cooking has been soaked to flavour and soften it.

clue.text: Old coward apt to retreat amid first signs of conflict and imminent fighting

indicators.note: amid puts the reversed word in among the initial letters
the first signs of words are their opening letters
retreating goes backwards, so this word is read from its end

parts.note: apt means fit, suitable

explanation.surface: A coward of old is inclined to withdraw when battle is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retreat' turns FIT into TIF, which goes amid CAIF.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a despicable craven person, a coward in old literature.

clue.text: Revolutionary time for youngster in service

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450

explanation.surface: A rebel has a spell as a young recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the Kentish revolt of 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee at a military or police academy is a young person entering the services.

clue.text: Neighbours initially coming in to gather round big fire

indicators.note: a letter coming in is entering between the other pieces

parts.note: to gather a conclusion is to infer it
O is round in shape

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Neighbours start arriving to crowd around a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A raging blaze, especially a huge destructive one, is a hellish conflagration.

clue.text: Shakespearean villain imprisoning male potential monarch

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding another piece within

parts.note: Iago is the villain of Othello

explanation.surface: Othello's schemer locks up a man who might become king.
explanation.walkthrough: A monarch is also a butterfly; the adult insect is its final form, so 'potential monarch' is wry.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult stage of an insect, as of a monarch butterfly, so a pupa's future form.

clue.text: Course warnings — attempt to get control over Oaks, say

parts.note: golfers shout fore as a warning on the course
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Shouts on the golf course and an effort to dominate the Oaks horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is an English horse race, but here oaks are trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Management of woodland, including oak trees, is the science of tending trees.

clue.text: Second duo appearing in act was hopeless

indicators.note: appearing in puts these pieces inside the act word

parts.note: an act is a deed
a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: A second double act on stage was a hopeless show.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lost all hope is to have given up in despondency.

clue.text: Dash to invest money in entertainment

indicators.note: to invest one thing in another is to put it inside
in completes the instruction, naming where the money goes

parts.note: a fair is a funfair, an entertainment
L stands for pound (libra), money

explanation.surface: A hurried plan to put cash into show business.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash as stylish verve or panache, a natural talent for style.

clue.text: Heather's morning departure from US

indicators.note: a departure from the country removes the letters from the word

parts.note: the US is America
AM is morning

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather leaves the States one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus of heaths and heather bears this Latin name.

clue.text: No riotous assembly has to move elsewhere? That's scandalous

indicators.note: an assembly puts the letters together in a new arrangement
the letters of the rowdy word must shift to new places, a second anagram signal

explanation.surface: No rowdy gathering should be forced to relocate; that would be outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'assembly' and 'has to move elsewhere' signal the rearrangement, fitting a crowd told to disperse; only one letter actually shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamous, well known for something bad, as with a scandalous reputation.

clue.text: Status and discipline leading to regular commission

indicators.note: the first piece leads, coming before the second

parts.note: standing is status
order is discipline

explanation.surface: Rank and discipline bring about a regular commission in the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: A bank's regular payment instruction; also a permanent rule of procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank instruction to pay a fixed sum at fixed intervals is a regular commission to act.

clue.text: Organise us a minder — for a small charge

definitions.text: Organise us a minder — for a small charge

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Get us a babysitter at a low fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organise' rearranges US A MINDER; 'a small charge' is a child in care, not a low fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after young children, so a minder of small charges.

clue.text: Cashier giving underworld boss payment

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
a charge is a payment

explanation.surface: A bank clerk paying a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' is a verb, to dismiss someone from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss him from the service.

clue.text: Hard to understand sailor's manoeuvre across entrance to tideway

indicators.note: the sailor's manoeuvre lies across the letter, spanning it

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; with the possessive s
a manoeuvre is a ruse, a trick

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A seaman's tactic across a river mouth is difficult to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite or obscure ideas are difficult to grasp.

clue.text: Double indemnity to secure cover for members

definitions.meaning: a doubled safeguard, extra precaution against failure
a waist strap and shoulder straps hold up trousers, which cover the legs or members

explanation.surface: A double insurance policy protects its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' are limbs, legs in trousers, not members of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Using two precautions where one would do, like holding trousers up two ways.

clue.text: American detained by courts in another country

indicators.note: detained by means held inside the courts word

parts.note: atria are courtyards
US is American

explanation.surface: An American held by foreign courts abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The central European republic is a country other than the American's own.

clue.text: Striker with a fantasy

parts.note: one who strikes bells is a chimer

explanation.surface: A footballer with a daydream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' looks like a footballer; it is a bell-ringer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild illusion or unrealistic dream, after the mythical fire-breathing monster.

clue.text: Carried out enquiry, with many put inside and charged

indicators.note: put inside places the letter within the other word

parts.note: pried means enquired nosily
M is a thousand in Roman numerals, many

explanation.surface: Police investigated, jailed many and pressed charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' means made ready, as a gun with powder, not accused.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded or made ready for action, as a gun prepared to fire.

clue.text: Appropriate heaps arranged to become well-defined structure

parts.note: to appropriate is to take

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Seize heaps sorted into a clear structure.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire a distinct form, to develop into a clear configuration.

clue.text: How to get bark finally to move slowly?

definitions.text: How to get bark finally to move slowly?

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

parts.note: to edge is to move slowly

explanation.surface: How to coax a dog's yap at last to inch along.
explanation.walkthrough: A bark is a sailing ship; to warp it along by hauling on a small anchor is how it moves slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul a ship forward by a dropped light anchor, moving it gradually.

clue.text: Something that divides the church? I'll say!

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: Someone splits the congregation? I'll say!
explanation.definitionFit: A passage between pews divides a church nave into sections.

clue.text: Some exotic horticulture producing a divine flower

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Unusual gardening yields a heavenly bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'producing', a link word; 'flower' is something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the ethereal fluid flowing in the gods' veins, so a godly liquid.

clue.text: It's subject to Articles in the European Community

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article
der is a German definite article

explanation.surface: Something that is bound by European Community legal articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beneath or governed by something, as in under orders.

clue.text: Percussion instrument appropriately included among the traps?

definitions.text: Percussion instrument appropriately included among the traps?

parts.words: Percussion instrument appropriately included among the traps?
parts.note: a drum kit is called the traps, and this drum's first word is itself a trap

explanation.surface: A drum fittingly belongs to the kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum with wires stretched beneath it, part of a drum kit.

clue.text: Raise tax, in general, by a quarter

indicators.note: by means beside, so the quarter sits next to the rest

parts.note: E, east, is a compass quarter

indicators.note: in puts the tax inside the general

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Increase tax generally by a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift or promote something to a higher level.

clue.text: Exhausted, pack study in — none pass here

indicators.note: to pack one thing into another is to stuff it inside
in completes the instruction, saying where the study goes

parts.note: dead means exhausted
a den is a study

explanation.surface: Worn out, I give up studying; nobody gets through.
explanation.definitionFit: A road closed at one end, so no traffic can go through.
